mainTopic: Moisture and חמץ in grain, soaking grain for פסח, and guarding (שימור) מצה from the start
overview: This עמוד deals with how grain can become חמץ through moisture, and how grain for מצה must be prepared. רב יוסף warns against boiling two wheat grains together, and אביי warns against roasting two stalks together. רבא answers that the grain's own liquid is מי פירות, and מי פירות do not cause leavening, and אביי retracts his stalk ruling. A ברייתא then forbids soaking barley on פסח. מר עוקבא and שמואל argue about what counts as 'split' grain, and שמואל rules against רבי יוסי's vinegar remedy. רבה, רב נחמן and רבא give different views on soaking grain. רבא first forbids it, then permits it, and finally says it is a מצוה, based on 'וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם אֶת הַמַּצּוֹת'. A proof from רב הונא's ruling about dough of גוים is pushed off, but רבא keeps his view. He has the grain handled לשם מצוה from the harvest onward. A story about מר בריה דרבינא begins, and it continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Do not boil two wheat grains together
steps.stepSummary: This finishes רב יוסף's rule, which began on the previous עמוד, that a person should not boil two wheat grains together. One grain might settle into the crease of the other and block the boiling water.
steps.simpleTranslation: [A person should not boil] two wheat grains together. One might move and settle into the crease of the other. Then the boiling water cannot reach the grain from all four sides, and it will become חמץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רב יוסף's rule, which started on the previous עמוד, against boiling two wheat grains at the same time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Boiling water cooks grain too fast for it to become חמץ, but only if the water touches every side. If one grain sits inside the crease of the other, that hidden spot is not hit by the boiling water. That spot is just wet and can leaven.

keyTerms.meaning: The slit or crease running along a wheat grain
The column or surge of boiling water

steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of a sentence. The words 'A person should not scald' (לא ליחלוט איניש) appear at the end of the previous עמוד.

phrases.english: [a person should not boil] two wheat grains together,
lest one of them move
and settle in the crease of the other,
and the surge of boiling water will not reach them
from all four sides,
and it will come to leavening.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב יוסף's statement begun on the previous עמוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two wheat grains should not be boiled together, because a spot hidden from the boiling water may leaven.

steps.title: Do not roast two stalks together
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds a second rule: a person should not roast two stalks of grain together. Liquid squeezed out of one stalk might soak into the other and make it חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי said: A person should not roast two stalks together. Liquid might come out of this one and be absorbed by the other, and it will become חמץ.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a new rule about roasting stalks of grain over fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When grain is heated, moisture comes out of it. אביי worries that this moisture acts like water: if it soaks into a neighboring stalk, that stalk could leaven. So he says to roast each stalk separately.

keyTerms.meaning: To roast or singe over fire

phrases.english: And Abaye said:
A person should not roast
two stalks together,
lest liquid come out of this one
and the other absorbs it,
and it comes to leavening.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, parallel rule from אביי about cooking grain on פסח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two stalks should not be roasted together, lest liquid from one leaven the other.

steps.title: רבא: then even one stalk should be forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges אביי's logic. If liquid moving from stalk to stalk is a problem, then liquid could also move from one end of a single stalk to its other end.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: If so, even one stalk should be forbidden too! Liquid might come out of this end and be absorbed by the other end!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's stalk rule by showing that the same worry would forbid roasting even a single stalk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's concern is about liquid traveling and soaking in somewhere else. That can happen within one stalk just as easily as between two. Since no one forbids roasting a single stalk, the worry must not be real.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that is your reasoning

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
If so, even one [stalk] as well [should be forbidden],
lest [liquid] come out of this end
and the other end absorbs it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning of אביי's stalk rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's rule against roasting two stalks together
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reductio ad absurdum: the same reasoning would forbid roasting even a single stalk, which is clearly allowed.

steps.title: רבא's view: grain liquid is fruit juice
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives his own reason why there is no worry at all. The liquid that comes out of grain is מי פירות, and מי פירות do not make grain חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: It is fruit juice, and fruit juice does not cause leavening.
steps.whatsHappening: After attacking אביי, רבא states his own principle that removes the concern entirely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only water causes grain to become חמץ. The moisture inside the grain itself counts as מי פירות, not water. So no matter where it drips, it cannot cause leavening.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit juice; liquid coming from produce itself rather than water

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule מי פירות אינן מחמיצין is a foundational principle in the laws of חמץ.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
It is fruit juice,
and fruit juice does not cause leavening.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's concern with רבא's own principle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liquid from grain is מי פירות, which does not cause leavening, so roasting stalks together is fine.

steps.title: אביי retracts his stalk ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that אביי took back his rule about two stalks. His reason: grain that is in the process of giving off moisture from the heat does not leaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי retracted from that ruling, because anything that is in the process of drawing out its moisture does not leaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us that אביי changed his mind about the stalks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי does not adopt רבא's מי פירות reason here. He gives his own reason: while the heat is actively drawing moisture out of the grain, it does not become חמץ. So the liquid passing between stalks over the fire is not a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: While they are giving off or drawing out moisture (from the heat)

steps.confusionAlert: אביי's retraction is based on his own reason (moisture being drawn out by heat), not on רבא's מי פירות principle. Their reasons stay different, as the next steps show.

phrases.english: And Abaye retracted from that [ruling about stalks],
because anything, while it is giving off its moisture,
does not leaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports the outcome of the debate over אביי's stalk rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אביי no longer forbids roasting two stalks together, since grain giving off moisture from heat does not leaven.

steps.title: אביי's jug ruling shows his later view
steps.stepSummary: To show אביי's revised view, the גמרא quotes his ruling about a jug used to roast grain. If the jug is upside down, it is permitted. If it stands upright, it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: As אביי said: Regarding a jug used for roasting grain, if it is turned upside down, it is permitted. If it is upright, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another statement of אביי as evidence for his position after the retraction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the jug is upside down, the moisture drips out while the grain is being heated, so nothing leavens. When it is upright, liquid can pool at the bottom and the grain can sit in it. אביי forbids only that case, which shows he is no longer worried about moisture passing between grains during heating.

phrases.english: As Abaye said:
This jug used for roasting grain,
if inverted, it is permitted;
if upright, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the report of אביי's retraction with another of his rulings.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's revised view that grain giving off moisture under heat does not leaven
steps.raayaSupportSource: אביי's ruling permitting an inverted jug of roasting grain and forbidding only an upright one

steps.title: רבא permits even an upright jug
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with אביי about the jug. Even an upright jug is permitted, because the liquid is מי פירות, which does not leaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even if it is upright, it is also permitted. It is fruit juice, and fruit juice does not cause leavening.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא states his opposing view on the jug case, using the same principle he used for the stalks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, it does not matter whether the liquid drips out or pools at the bottom. Either way, it is the grain's own liquid, so it is מי פירות and cannot cause חמץ. This is where אביי and רבא still disagree.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי retracted his worry about two stalks, but he still forbids an upright jug where liquid pools. רבא permits everything, because grain liquid is מי פירות and מי פירות אינן מחמיצין.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Even if upright, it is also permitted;
it is fruit juice,
and fruit juice does not cause leavening.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר אֲפִילּוּ זְקִיפָא נָמֵי שְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with אביי's jug ruling in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An upright jug of roasting grain is also permitted, since the liquid is מי פירות.

steps.title: ברייתא: do not soak barley on פסח
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא opens a new topic. Barley should not be soaked in water on פסח, but if it was soaked, it is forbidden only if the grains split.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: One may not soak barley on פסח. If one did soak it, then if the grains split, they are forbidden. If they did not split, they are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about soaking barley (to loosen the husks) on פסח. This opens a new discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Soaking grain in water risks חמץ, so it should not be done from the start. After the fact, splitting is the sign that leavening began. If the grains did not split, they may be used.

keyTerms.meaning: Soaking grain in water to loosen the husks

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One may not soak barley on Passover.
And if one soaked them: if they split, they are forbidden;
if they did not split, they are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן אֵין לוֹתְתִין שְׂעוֹרִין בַּפֶּסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic: soaking barley on פסח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Barley should not be soaked on פסח. After the fact, it is forbidden only if the grains split.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: vinegar can stop the grain from leavening
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with רבי יוסי's view: grain that is starting to swell can be soaked in vinegar, and the vinegar shrinks it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: One soaks them in vinegar, and the vinegar shrinks them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the last step continues. רבי יוסי offers a fix: if barley is starting to swell, put it in vinegar to stop it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion said soaked barley is forbidden only once it splits. רבי יוסי adds a remedy before that point: vinegar tightens the grain, so it will not reach the leavening stage.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
He soaks them in vinegar,
phrases.notes: This applies to barley that is beginning to swell.

phrases.english: and the vinegar shrinks them.
phrases.notes: Vinegar firms up the grain, so it does not leaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second opinion inside the same ברייתא quoted in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Swelling barley may be put in vinegar, which stops it from leavening.

steps.title: שמואל rules against רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that the הלכה does not follow רבי יוסי's vinegar remedy.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: The הלכה is not like רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the final ruling on the argument in the ברייתא. We do not rely on vinegar to save swelling grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי held that vinegar can rescue grain that has started to swell. שמואל rejects this in practice, so we do not trust the vinegar to fully stop leavening.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law is not (like this view)

steps.whatToRemember: Practically, we do not use vinegar to save swelling grain. The הלכה is not like רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
The halakha is not like Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the practical law on רבי יוסי's view from step 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The vinegar remedy is not accepted in practice.

steps.title: מר עוקבא: 'split' includes grain that is about to split
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא reports in the name of מר עוקבא that 'split' does not require a real crack. It includes grain that would split by itself if placed on the mouth of a wine barrel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of מר עוקבא: 'Split' does not mean actually split. Rather, it means any grain that, if you placed it on the mouth of a barrel, would split by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא's word 'split' and asks how far along the grain must be. מר עוקבא gives a broad definition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this view, a visible crack is not needed. If the grain is so swollen that the vapor of a wine barrel would make it burst, it already counts as split and is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said that Mar Ukva said:
'They split' does not mean actually split,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כׇּל שֶׁאִילּוּ מַנִּיחָן עַל פִּי חָבִית
phrases.english: rather, any grains that, if one placed them on the mouth of a barrel,
phrases.notes: This refers to a barrel of wine, whose vapor affects the grain.

phrases.english: would split by themselves.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the key word 'split' in the ברייתא from step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Grain that is on the verge of splitting already counts as split and is forbidden.

steps.title: שמואל: only grain that really split is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees with מר עוקבא and says 'split' means actually split.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: It means actually split.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the opposite definition. Only a real, visible split makes the grain forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a narrower reading than מר עוקבא's. Grain that is only close to splitting is still permitted, according to שמואל.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: It means they actually split.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with מר עוקבא's definition in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only barley with a real split is forbidden.

steps.title: שמואל ruled this way in a real case
steps.stepSummary: שמואל acted on his view in the village of בר חשו and forbade only grain that had truly split.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל made a practical ruling in the village of the house of בר חשו: only grains that actually split were forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing that שמואל really followed his view in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A practical ruling (מעשה) shows that שמואל's view was not just theory. He permitted grain that was only close to splitting.

keyTerms.meaning: He made a practical ruling / acted on it

phrases.english: Shmuel acted on this in practice
in the village of the house of bar Ḥashu:
he forbade only those that actually split.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows שמואל applying his view from step 12.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's view that only grain that really split is forbidden
steps.raayaSupportSource: A practical ruling by שמואל in the village of בר חשו

steps.title: רבה: a pious person should not soak grain
steps.stepSummary: רבה says that a בעל נפש should not soak grain on פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: A בעל נפש should not soak.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה adds an extra stringency for especially careful people: do not soak grain at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes beyond the basic law. It is advice for someone who wants to be extra careful about חמץ. The next step asks what exactly it adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Should soak (grain in water before grinding)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה: בַּעַל נֶפֶשׁ לֹא יִלְתּוֹת.
phrases.english: Rabba said: A pious person should not soak.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: בַּעַל נֶפֶשׁ לֹא יִלְתּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a pious stringency to the topic of soaking from step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בעל נפש should avoid soaking grain.

steps.title: Why only a pious person? Everyone is told not to soak barley
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבה limits this to a בעל נפש. The ברייתא already says no one may soak barley on פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why specifically a בעל נפש? Even everyone should not soak, as it was taught: One may not soak barley on פסח!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבה's statement. If the ברייתא already forbids everyone, the 'pious' advice seems to add nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא from step 8 tells everyone not to soak barley. So a rule just for the pious makes no sense, unless it means something more.

phrases.english: Why specifically a pious person?
Even everyone else too should not,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא תַּנְיָא: אֵין לוֹתְתִין שְׂעוֹרִין בַּפֶּסַח!
phrases.english: as it was taught: One may not soak barley on Passover!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of רבה's statement in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's limiting of the rule to a בעל נפש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids everyone to soak barley, so a special rule for the pious seems pointless.

steps.title: A pious person avoids soaking even firm wheat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבה means a בעל נפש should not soak even wheat, which is firmer than barley.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: A בעל נפש should not soak even wheat, which is firm.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by explaining what רבה really meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone avoids soaking barley, because it is soft and splits easily. רבה's extra point is about wheat: it is hard and less likely to leaven, so it is allowed by law, but a pious person avoids soaking it too.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying: A pious person
should not soak even wheat, which is firm.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the subject of the statement (wheat, not barley)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבה was talking about barley, which everyone may not soak.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבה is talking about wheat, which is permitted by law, but a pious person avoids soaking it.

steps.title: רב נחמן: following רבה leads to poor bread
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן objects to רבה: anyone who listens to him will eat poor-quality bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: Whoever listens to אבא (that is, רבה) will eat moldy bread.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן pushes back on רבה's pious stringency. He says it has a bad practical result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Soaking cleans the grain and removes the husks. Without it, the bread comes out coarse and poor, so רב נחמן says avoiding soaking is not a good practice.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said to him:
Whoever listens to Abba
will eat moldy bread.
phrases.notes: Unsoaked grain keeps its husks, so the bread is coarse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Objects to רבה's pious stringency as explained in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's advice that a pious person should not soak grain
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Avoiding soaking gives poor bread, so it is not a worthy practice.

steps.title: Great houses did soak their grain
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן supports his objection: the households of רב הונא and רבא בר אבין soaked their grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: For in the house of רב הונא they soaked, and in the house of רבא בר אבין they soaked.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן brings practical proof that important rabbis allowed soaking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If great and careful rabbis soaked their grain, then avoiding it is not needed even for the pious. This supports רב נחמן against רבה.

phrases.english: For in Rav Huna's house they would soak,
and in Rava bar Avin's house they would soak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives support for רב נחמן's objection in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That soaking grain is a proper practice
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice in the households of רב הונא and רבא בר אבין

steps.title: רבא: soaking is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבא takes the strictest view: it is forbidden to soak grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: It is forbidden to soak.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a third view. Soaking is not just something pious people avoid; it is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן allows soaking, and רבה avoids it only as piety. רבא makes it a real prohibition, out of fear that the grain will leaven.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבה (step 14) with רבא (this step). They are different אמוראים. רבה said only a pious person avoids soaking, while רבא says soaking is forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three views on soaking grain. רב נחמן says it is fine. רבה says a pious person avoids it. רבא says it is forbidden.

phrases.english: And Rava said: It is forbidden to soak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A stricter opinion set against both רבה and רב נחמן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Soaking grain for פסח is forbidden.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to allow soaking wheat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's ban on soaking. A ברייתא forbids soaking barley, which seems to imply that soaking wheat is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the ברייתא that teaches: 'One may not soak barley on פסח'? That suggests only barley is forbidden, while wheat is permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא, who just said that soaking any grain is forbidden. A ברייתא mentions only barley, which suggests that wheat may be soaked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא forbade soaking all grain. The ברייתא names only barley, so a reader would infer that wheat is fine. That inference contradicts רבא's blanket ban, and the גמרא wants to know how רבא explains it.

phrases.english: But that which was taught in a baraita:
One may not soak barley on Passover.
It is barley that one may not soak,
phrases.notes: The גמרא is inferring from what the ברייתא leaves out.

phrases.english: but wheat is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling from step 19 that soaking is forbidden.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that soaking any grain is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By naming only barley, the ברייתא implies that wheat may be soaked. That contradicts a total ban.

steps.title: The ברייתא means 'needless to say wheat, even barley'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא uses a 'לא מיבעיא' style. Wheat obviously may not be soaked because water enters its crease. Barley is smooth, so one might have thought it is allowed, and the ברייתא teaches that it is forbidden too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא is saying 'needless to say.' Needless to say wheat is forbidden, since it has a crease and water gets inside. But barley is smooth, so you might say soaking it is fine. The ברייתא teaches us that it is forbidden too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא. The ברייתא mentions barley not to permit wheat, but because barley is the less obvious case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wheat has a crease where water can seep in and start leavening, so forbidding it is obvious. Barley is smooth and seems to resist water, so a person might think it is allowed. The ברייתא chose the less obvious case to show that even barley is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Needless to say (teaching the less obvious case)
A crease or slit in the grain

steps.confusionAlert: Back in step 16, wheat was called firmer than barley. Here wheat is treated as the more vulnerable grain because water enters its crease. These are two different angles on the grains, so do not mix them up.

phrases.english: It is speaking in a 'needless to say' style.
Needless to say wheat may not be soaked,
since it has a slit,
water enters it,
but barley, which is smooth,
I might say it is fine to soak,
so it teaches us that it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 20 by reinterpreting how the ברייתא is phrased.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the ברייתא's style (לא מיבעיא), so its silence about wheat no longer implies permission.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mentioning only barley means wheat is permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: Barley was chosen as the less obvious case. Wheat is forbidden all the more.

steps.title: רבא changes his mind and permits soaking
steps.stepSummary: רבא retracts his earlier ban and rules that soaking grain is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא then said: It is permitted to soak grain.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא reverses his earlier ruling and now permits soaking. His proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, רבא forbade soaking all grain. Now he says soaking is allowed. This sets up the proof that follows.

phrases.english: Rava reconsidered and said:
It is permitted to soak grain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses רבא's own ruling from step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Soaking grain for מצה is permitted.

steps.title: Proof: refined מצה is valid, and refining requires soaking
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a ברייתא saying one fulfills the מצוה with refined bread. Refined flour cannot be made without soaking, so soaking must be allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: One fulfills the obligation with refined bread and with coarse bread. And refined bread is impossible without soaking.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא proves his new ruling. The ברייתא allows refined מצה, and refined flour needs soaking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא approves refined flour for מצה. Making refined flour requires soaking the grain to remove the husk fully. So the ברייתא must assume that soaking is allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This claim, that refined flour is impossible without soaking, is exactly what רב פפא attacks next.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
One fulfills the obligation with refined bread and with coarse bread,
and refined bread is impossible without soaking.
phrases.notes: This is רבא's own reasoning added to the ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the proof for רבא's new ruling in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that soaking is permitted
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא approving refined bread for מצה, combined with the claim that refining requires soaking.

steps.title: רב פפא cites a ברייתא about flour of גוים
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא brings a ברייתא: flour of גוים from villages is טהור, while flour from big cities is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא objected to רבא: Flour and fine flour belonging to גוים: if from villages, it is pure; if from cities, it is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא begins a challenge to רבא by quoting a ברייתא. This is the setup, and the actual point of the challenge comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food can become טמא only after it has gotten wet (הכשר). City flour is assumed to come from soaked grain, so it is wet, susceptible, and made טמא by the גוים. Village flour is טהור, which hints that its grain was never soaked.
steps.confusionAlert: Why does soaking matter for טומאה? Food can only become טמא after contact with water. Soaked grain got wet, so it can become impure. Unsoaked grain cannot.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa raised an objection to Rava:
Flours and fine flours of gentiles,
those of villages are pure,
and those of cities are impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins attacking the proof in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that refined flour is impossible without soaking
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sets up a ברייתא that will show refined flour existing without soaking.

steps.title: Village flour is unsoaked yet called refined
steps.stepSummary: Village flour is טהור because it was not soaked, yet the ברייתא calls it סולת. So refined flour can be made without soaking, which undercuts רבא's proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is village flour pure? Isn't it because they don't soak it? And yet the ברייתא calls it fine flour!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא completes his challenge. Unsoaked village flour is still called refined, so רבא's claim that refining requires soaking is wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Village flour stays טהור only because it never got wet, meaning it was not soaked. Yet the ברייתא includes it under סלתות, fine flour. So refined flour exists without soaking, and רבא's proof falls apart.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא permitted soaking because refined מצה supposedly requires it. רב פפא shows from village flour that refined flour can be made without soaking.

phrases.english: Those of villages, what is the reason they are pure?
Is it not because they do not soak,
and yet it calls it fine flour!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the ברייתא in step 24 that completes the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's statement 'אי אפשר נקיה בלא לתיתה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Unsoaked village flour is still called סולת, so refined flour can be made without soaking.

steps.title: רבא says the village-flour teaching is about plain flour
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers רב פפא: the ברייתא about village flour being טהור refers to ordinary flour (קמח), not to refined flour (סולת).
steps.simpleTranslation: Explain it as referring to ordinary flour.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his proof by saying the village flour in the ברייתא is plain flour, not refined flour.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא had argued that refined flour can be made without soaking, because village flour is unsoaked and yet is called סולת. רבא answers that the ruling of טהור applies only to ordinary flour. Refined flour always needs soaking, so it would always be able to become טמא. That keeps רבא's proof alive.

phrases.english: Interpret it as referring to ordinary flour.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא's distinction is limited to ordinary flour.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge from Step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the source: the ברייתא is about ordinary flour, not refined flour.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The village flour in the ברייתא included סולת, so סולת can be made without soaking.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only ordinary flour is unsoaked and טהור. סולת still requires soaking.

steps.title: רב פפא's afterthought: meal-offering wheat is called refined flour without soaking
steps.stepSummary: After רבא left, רב פפא said he should have challenged him from שמואל: wheat for מנחות is not soaked, yet it is called סולת.
steps.simpleTranslation: After he left, he said: Why didn't I tell him this teaching that רבי זירא said in the name of רב ירמיה in the name of שמואל: Wheat for meal-offerings is not soaked, yet it is called refined flour?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא brings a stronger challenge that רבא's answer cannot dodge. A source that calls unsoaked wheat סולת directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's answer in Step 26 claimed that סולת always needs soaking. שמואל's teaching shows that the wheat for מנחות is never soaked, and the Torah still calls it סולת. So refined flour can exist without soaking, and רבא's proof from refined bread falls apart again.

keyTerms.meaning: After he went out (after רבא left)
Flour offerings brought in the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not arguing with רבא face to face here. He is saying afterward what he should have answered. The point still counts as a real challenge to רבא's answer.

phrases.english: After he (רבא) left, he (רב פפא) said:
Why didn't I say to him
from this teaching that רבי זירא said
that רב ירמיה said that שמואל said:

phrases.aramaic: חִיטִּין שֶׁל מְנָחוֹת אֵין לוֹתְתִין אוֹתָם,
phrases.english: Wheat for meal-offerings: we do not soak it,
and yet it is called refined flour.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אֵימָא לֵיהּ מֵהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Undercuts רבא's answer in Step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that refined flour (סולת) always requires soaking.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The flour for מנחות is never soaked, yet it is called סולת. So soaking is not needed to make סולת, and רבא's proof from refined bread fails.

steps.title: רבא now rules that soaking is a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רבא changes his position again and says it is a מצוה to soak the grain, based on the פסוק "וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם אֶת הַמַּצּוֹת".
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא then said: It is a מצוה to soak, as it says: "And you shall guard the מצות."
steps.whatsHappening: רבא makes a new and stronger ruling: soaking is not just allowed, it is a מצוה. He gives a פסוק as his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, רבא had only argued that soaking is permitted, and his proof was knocked down. Now he goes further and says soaking is a מצוה. His source is the Torah's command to guard the מצות. The next step explains how the פסוק shows this.

keyTerms.meaning: He then said, he changed his position
And you shall guard the מצות (שמות יב:יז)

phrases.english: רבא then said:
It is a מצוה to soak,
as it says: "And you shall guard the מצות."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After his proof was rejected, רבא gives a new position and a new source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Soaking grain for מצה is a מצוה, learned from "וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם אֶת הַמַּצּוֹת".
steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the question. It is no longer only whether soaking is allowed. Now soaking is actually part of how the מצוה of guarding the מצה is done.

steps.title: Guarding only makes sense if it covers soaking
steps.stepSummary: If there were no soaking, there would be nothing for the guarding to apply to. Guarding at the kneading stage does not count as guarding.
steps.simpleTranslation: If soaking were not needed, what would the guarding be for? If you say it means guarding during kneading, guarding during kneading is not considered guarding.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the פסוק proves that soaking is a מצוה. It rules out the idea that the guarding refers to the kneading stage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah commands a special guarding of the מצות, so it must refer to a stage where grain could become חמץ, and soaking is such a stage. One might say it refers to kneading. But the גמרא says guarding at kneading does not count as the Torah's guarding. So the guarding must begin earlier, at soaking.

keyTerms.meaning: Guarding the grain or dough from becoming חמץ

phrases.english: If soaking were not required,
what would the guarding be for?
If you say it means guarding at kneading,
guarding at kneading is not considered guarding.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָא דְּבָעֵי לְתִיתָה שִׁימּוּר לְמַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק in Step 28 proves רבא's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: That the guarding of מצות begins at soaking, so soaking is a מצוה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The command "וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם אֶת הַמַּצּוֹת", together with the rule that guarding at kneading does not count.

steps.title: רב הונא: one may eat dough of גוים but must finish with real מצה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that a person may fill himself with dough made by גוים on פסח night, as long as he eats a כזית of מצה at the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב הונא said: Dough of גוים, a person may fill his stomach with it, as long as he eats a כזית of מצה at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב הונא's ruling as the source for the claim that guarding at kneading does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dough made by גוים that did not become חמץ may be eaten on פסח. But רב הונא requires a separate כזית of proper מצה at the end. That shows the dough of גוים does not count for the מצוה of eating מצה. The next steps explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive-sized amount, the minimum for the מצוה

phrases.english: As רב הונא said:
Dough of non-Jews:
a person may fill his stomach with them,
provided that he eats a כזית of מצה at the end.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind the claim in Step 29.
steps.raayaObject: That guarding which starts late does not count as שימור for מצה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב הונא's ruling about dough of גוים.

steps.title: Why doesn't the gentiles' dough count for the מצוה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from רב הונא that the מצה at the end counts but the dough of גוים eaten at first does not, and it asks why.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the end, yes. At the beginning, no. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads רב הונא's words closely and asks what is wrong with the dough of גוים. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "at the end" imply that only the final כזית of proper מצה fulfills the מצוה. The dough of גוים eaten earlier does not. The גמרא now wants to know what this dough is missing.

phrases.english: At the end, yes. At the beginning, no.
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from רב הונא's words and asks for the reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the dough of גוים does not fulfill the מצוה of eating מצה.

steps.title: Because no guarding was done
steps.stepSummary: The dough of גוים does not count because no שימור was done with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he did not guard them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the dough is missing proper guarding, so it cannot be used for the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To fulfill the מצוה of eating מצה, the מצה must be guarded. The גוי who made this dough did not guard it for the sake of the מצוה. So the dough does not count, even though it may be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not do with them

phrases.english: Because he did not do guarding with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dough of גוים lacks שימור, so it cannot fulfill the מצוה.

steps.title: He could still guard it from baking onward
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: why not let the Jew guard the dough from baking onward and fulfill the מצוה that way?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him do guarding with it from baking onward!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the point: the Jew could still guard the dough at a later stage. This sets up the final conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If late guarding counted, the dough of גוים could be fixed by guarding it from baking onward. Yet רב הונא still requires separate מצה. So late guarding must not be enough, and this leads to the conclusion in the next step.

phrases.english: But let him do guarding with it from baking onward!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the simple reading of the answer in Step 32 in order to sharpen it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that guarding can be added at a later stage.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If late guarding were enough, the dough of גוים could be guarded from baking and then used for the מצוה. רב הונא does not allow this, so the gap must be explained.

steps.title: Proposed proof: guarding is required from the very beginning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that שימור must begin from the start, which supports רבא's ruling that soaking is a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it correct to learn from this: we need guarding from the very beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its proposed proof: proper guarding must start from the beginning, not partway through. The next step rejects this proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If late guarding does not count, then the guarding the Torah commands must start early, at the soaking stage. That would support רבא's point that soaking is a מצוה. The next step questions whether the dough of גוים really proves this.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it so? Learn from this

steps.whatToRemember: This proof from רב הונא's ruling about dough of גוים seems to show that שימור must begin from the start. The next step rejects the proof, and step 36 shows that רבא kept his view anyway.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it so? Learn from this:
we require guarding from the very beginning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the push in Step 33 and completes the proof for Step 28.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The proposed inference is that שימור is required from the very beginning. The next step rejects this proof.

steps.title: The proof from dough of גוים is pushed off
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof for רבא. Dough of גוים may fail only because no one guarded it at the time of kneading. Guarding that starts at kneading might still be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: But how do you know? Maybe the dough of גוים is different. At the moment guarding is needed, when water touches the flour, no guarding was done at all. But where guarding is done at that moment, maybe guarding from kneading does count as real guarding.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from Step 34. It says the case of dough made by גוים does not really show that guarding must start before kneading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 34 argued that because a Jew cannot fix the dough of גוים by guarding it later, guarding must begin at the very start. The rejection points out a different reason that dough fails: at kneading, when water first touches the flour and the danger of חמץ begins, nobody was guarding it. So the case leaves open the possibility that guarding which starts at kneading is good enough.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where (do you know)? This opens a challenge to a proof.
Perhaps. It offers another way to explain the case.
It is different there. The case may have its own special reason.
Kneading, the stage when water is added to flour.

steps.confusionAlert: This step does NOT say guarding from kneading is enough. It only says this proof fails. Step 36 shows that רבא kept his view anyway.

phrases.english: And from where (do we know this)?
phrases.notes: Here the גמרא starts pushing back on the proof.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is different there,
phrases.notes: There refers to the dough of gentiles.

phrases.english: for at the time when guarding becomes required,
phrases.notes: That is, when water is added to the flour.

phrases.english: he did not guard it.
But where, at the time when guarding becomes required,
he does guard it,

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי דְּשִׁימּוּר דְּלִישָׁה הָוֵי שִׁימּוּר.
phrases.english: so too, guarding from kneading would count as guarding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the support for רבא that was drawn in Step 34.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. The halacha itself is not overturned.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Dough of גוים had no guarding at all at the key moment of kneading. So it cannot prove that guarding which starts at kneading is too late.

steps.title: רבא keeps his view and has the grain harvested for the sake of the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: Even with the proof rejected, רבא did not back down. He told the harvesters to work on the grain לשם מצוה. This shows he holds that שימור is needed from the very beginning until the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, רבא did not take back his view. He told the workers who were turning over the sheaves: when you turn them over, do it for the sake of the מצוה. This shows he holds that we need guarding from the start, from the beginning all the way to the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us that losing the proof did not change רבא's position. It brings his practice in the field as evidence of what he held.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא did not just start guarding at kneading. He began at the harvest, with the cutting and turning of the stalks. That practice shows he requires שימור לשם מצוה from the earliest stage of the grain until the מצה is baked. The proof was weakened, but רבא's practice still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not retract or change his mind.
Those turning over the sheaves or stalks. Some explain it as cutting and binding the grain.
For the sake of the מצוה.
Apparently, which shows that. It introduces an inference.
From its beginning until its end.

steps.whatToRemember: רבא holds that שימור for מצה must be done לשם מצוה from the harvest of the grain until the baking. This holds even though the proof from dough of גוים was rejected.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a source for the practice of מצה שמורה guarded from the time of harvest (שמורה משעת קצירה).

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ הָכִי לָא הֲדַר בֵּיהּ רָבָא.
phrases.english: And even so, Rava did not retract.
For he said to those who were turning over the sheaves:
phrases.notes: Workers handling the harvested stalks in the field.

phrases.english: When you turn them over, turn them over for the sake of the מצוה.
Apparently he holds:

phrases.aramaic: שִׁימּוּר מֵעִיקָּרָא מִתְּחִלָּתוֹ וְעַד סוֹפוֹ בָּעֵינַן.
phrases.english: we require guarding from the outset, from its beginning until its end.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ הָכִי לָא הֲדַר בֵּיהּ רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof is rejected in Step 35, the גמרא shows that רבא still kept his position.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא requires שימור לשם מצוה from the start of the grain's processing, beginning at the harvest, all the way to the end.

steps.title: Opening a new story about מר בריה דרבינא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new report about how מר בריה דרבינא guarded his grain. The report continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר, the son of רבינא...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is starting to tell what מר בריה דרבינא did, and the details come on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After establishing רבא's view, the גמרא turns to another אמורא's practice in guarding grain for מצה. Only the name appears here. The content of the story follows right after.

phrases.english: Mar, son of Ravina,
phrases.notes: The story continues on the next עמוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבא's practice to another אמורא's practice on the same topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated. This only introduces the practice of מר בריה דרבינא.
